premise: Deciding to fly a single-engine monoplane across the treacherous Atlantic Ocean without a parachute or radio.
hook: He stripped his custom aircraft of every ounce of excess weight—including the radio—to bet his life on a nonstop flight to Paris.
key_facts: Flew the custom-built Spirit of St. Louis from Roosevelt Field, New York, to Paris in May 1927.
Completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 33.5 hours.
Flew without a forward-facing windshield, relying on a periscope to see ahead.
Became an instant global aviation icon upon landing at Le Bourget Airport.

premise: Co-founding Infosys with just $250 borrowed from his wife, growing it into a global IT giant.
hook: He started a multinational tech powerhouse from a spare bedroom with a minuscule loan and a borrowed dining table.
key_facts: Started Infosys in Pune, India, in 1981 with six other software engineers.
Relied on initial seed capital provided by his wife, Sudha Murthy, from her personal savings.
Pioneered the global delivery model for software services out of India.

premise: Choosing not to patent the polio vaccine, ensuring it remained freely accessible globally.
hook: He was asked who owned the patent to the vaccine that saved millions, and his answer shocked the corporate world.
key_facts: Developed the first safe and effective polio vaccine in the early 1950s.
Announced the vaccine's success publicly on national radio in 1955.
Chose not to patent the discovery, stating that the patent belonged to the people.

premise: Inventing a completely unorthodox, backward jumping technique that revolutionized high jumping forever.
hook: Every high jumper in the world cleared the bar facing down, until a frustrated college student decided to jump backward over his head.
key_facts: Pioneered the 'Fosbury Flop' technique at Oregon State University in the late 1960s.
Won the gold medal using his revolutionary technique at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City.
Permanently changed how modern athletes approach the high jump event.

premise: Inventing the microwave oven after a candy bar melted in his pocket while working near a magnetron tube.
hook: He was standing next to a military radar radar tube when the peanut cluster in his shirt pocket began to bubble and cook.
key_facts: Worked as an engineer for the Raytheon Corporation during World War II.
Noticed that electromagnetic waves from a magnetron had melted a snack in his pocket.
Patented the first commercial microwave oven, known as the Radarange, in 1947.

premise: Rising from a public housing project in Brooklyn to transform a small regional coffee bean shop into Starbucks.
hook: He watched his father lose his job after a workplace injury, vowing to build a company that treated working people with dignity.
key_facts: Grew up in the Bayview housing projects in Brooklyn, New York.
Joined Starbucks as the director of marketing when it had only a handful of stores.
Acquired the company in 1987 and expanded it into a global cafe franchise.
